subject: Editing axis text and expanding color scale in filled histogram

messages.author: d7a43f3c8dc40522
messages.subject: Editing axis text and expanding color scale in filled histogram
parts:
A while ago I got your help to color my faceted histograms by a
specific value, like this:

d2 <- merge(diamonds, aggregate(carat~color, mean, data=diamonds),
by="color", suffix=c("", ".mean"))

ggplot(d2,aes(x=carat, fill=carat.mean)) + geom_histogram() +
facet_grid(cut~color) + scale_fill_gradient(low="orange", high="blue")

the means are here like this:
> summary(d2$carat.mean)
Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max.
0.6578 0.6579 0.7712 0.7979 0.9118 1.1620
>

The color scheme goes from 1.7 to 1.1, thus excluding the outer limit
of the actual range. I have tried adding limits to the
scale_fill_gradient, by adding limits=c(0.6,1.2), but then, while 0.6
does get a nice color, 1.2 does not.

How do I fix this?

Also, as you can see from the same figure, I have counts on the side
that in this case goes from 0 to 1000. In my real life plot I have
counts going up to 2500. I was wondering if there was a way that I
could have this as numbers * 100, i.e. in this case, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and
10.

TIA!

>  0.6578  0.6579  0.7712  0.7979  0.9118  1.1620
>>
>
> The color scheme goes from 1.7 to 1.1, thus excluding the outer limit

> scale_fill_gradient, by adding limits=c(0.6,1.2), but then, while 0.6

I think the problem is even worse than this. None of the values are correct.

I think something like

ggplot(d2,aes(x=carat, fill=factor(round(carat.mean, digits=2)))) +
geom_histogram() +
facet_grid(cut~color) +
scale_fill_hue("Mean carat")

is a more accurate display.

>
> Also, as you can see from the same figure, I have counts on the side
> that in this case goes from 0 to 1000. In my real life plot I have
> counts going up to 2500. I was wondering if there was a way that I
> could have this as numbers * 100, i.e. in this case, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and
> 10.

scale_y_continuous("Count \n(in hundreds)", breaks=seq(0,1000,
by=200), labels=c(seq(0,10, by=2)))

HTH,
Ista
